subject.title: Granola 7.427.2 moved the DEK from storage.dek into the macOS Keychain — encrypted-json/private-api unlock fails with "read storage.dek: no such file or directory"

question: Should Graincrawl stop at a clear unsupported-Keychain diagnostic, or pursue an authorized Granola companion or bridge for the access-group-protected DEK?
rationale: The new DEK is reportedly protected by another application’s data-protection Keychain access group, so selecting a retrieval mechanism affects signing, authorization, distribution, and Graincrawl’s documented trust boundary.

options.title: Diagnostic now, bridge later
options.body: Add precise detection and classification immediately, while requiring an upstream-authorized interface before restoring encrypted decryption.

options.title: Authorized companion integration
options.body: Coordinate on a Granola-provided CLI or app bridge, then integrate it after its authorization and threat model are documented.

options.title: Retire encrypted unlock
options.body: Declare Keychain-backed encrypted JSON unsupported and direct users to maintained plaintext or other supported source paths.

recommendation.title: Diagnostic now, bridge later
recommendation.body: Add precise detection and classification immediately, while requiring an upstream-authorized interface before restoring encrypted decryption.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant repository security contract and encrypted-source design trace most directly to this feature area.
